title: Gotcha Force
subtitle: A toy collection becomes a fighting force
summary: Gotcha Force is Capcom's arena action game, first released for GameCube in Japan on 27 November 2003.
body: Gotcha Force is Capcom's arena action game, first released for GameCube in Japan on 27 November 2003. Children command teams of miniature Gotcha Borgs, collectible fighters whose different weapons and abilities turn small everyday environments into battlegrounds. The story follows Kou and his allies against the Death Force. Collecting and fighting are closely linked: a newly obtained Borg changes the possible lineup, while another match gives the player a chance to discover how that fighter behaves when placed against a moving opponent.

Before a battle, the commander builds a force within a GF Energy allowance. More powerful Borgs consume more of that budget, creating a choice between a few expensive fighters and a larger sequence of cheaper ones. In the arena, lock-on targeting keeps the opponent in view while movement, jumps and attacks determine how to approach. Some Borgs specialise in close combat, others fire from a distance or support an ally. The collection matters because its members produce different tactical possibilities rather than simply another appearance.

When one Borg is defeated, the next member of the force enters and continues the battle. A good lineup therefore considers both individual strength and the order in which different abilities become available. Multiplayer lets players bring those decisions into matches with friends, while the campaign expands the roster through repeated encounters. Mitsuhiko Takano composed the music. The game's lasting appeal centres on this link between a crowded toy collection and the very specific fighting style of the next small character sent into the arena.
